info.description:
The HTTP API behind the Pursuit dashboard and the `pursuit` CLI. Agents should prefer the CLI: `pursuit schema <command>` describes one command. The short agent guide is [/llms.txt](/llms.txt).

## Authentication

Send `Authorization: Bearer pst_...`. A token holds the scopes `read`, `write`, and `approve`. `write` does not include `approve`, and only `approve` can move an application toward submission. Tokens, scopes, and OAuth login are in [/auth.md](/auth.md).

## Errors

Errors are JSON: `{"error": {"code", "message", "hint", "details"}}`. 400 is validation, 401 a missing or bad token, 403 a missing scope, 404 not found, 409 a version or cap conflict.

## Writes

Every write accepts `Idempotency-Key`, which replays a successful response, and `X-Dry-Run: true`, which validates and writes nothing. Updates and deletes of versioned records take `version` in the body, the query, or `If-Match`.

## Pagination

Lists take `limit` (1-200) and `cursor`, and return `next_cursor` until the last page. `POST /v1/batch` runs up to 100 requests in one call.

post.description: RFC 8628 device authorization for pursuit auth login --device. Scope is space or comma separated, each exactly read or write, default read write; anything else (approve, APPROVE, Read) is invalid_scope: OAuth never grants approve. client_id is at most 64 characters. Limited to 10 starts a minute per client IP (429 slow_down). Device codes last 10 minutes; poll /v1/auth/token no faster than interval. There is no verification_uri_complete: the human types the code.

Body {}. Returns {publicKey} for PublicKeyCredential.parseRequestOptionsFromJSON with no allowCredentials, so nothing reveals which accounts exist. The challenge is single-use and lasts 5 minutes. 404 when passkeys are off (PURSUIT_WEBAUTHN_RP_ID unset). Requires Content-Type application/json and Sec-Fetch-Site same-origin or a matching Origin. Begin and finish together are limited to 20 a minute per client IP (429).

Body is the browser's PublicKeyCredential.toJSON(). Verifies challenge, origin, RP ID, signature, user verification and sign count, then mints a pst_ login token (name login, read,write,approve) into the httpOnly pursuit_session cookie and answers like GET /v1/me. Never creates a user: an unknown, removed or replayed passkey is 401. Same-origin JSON only.

post.description: RFC 7009 token revocation. Holding the token is the authority; unknown tokens still return 200. `pursuit auth logout` calls this.

delete.description: Clear the pursuit_session cookie and revoke it when sign-in minted it (token name login). Any other token stays valid; revoke it with POST /v1/auth/revoke. Same-origin only; returns 204.

post.description: Verify a token (pst_, or a Better Auth JWT exchanged for a pst_ login token) and store the pst_ token in the httpOnly pursuit_session cookie, then answer like GET /v1/me. Requires Content-Type application/json and Sec-Fetch-Site same-origin or a matching Origin. Body {token}. Agents send Authorization: Bearer instead.

OAuth2 token endpoint. grant_type=authorization_code takes code, code_verifier (PKCE S256), redirect_uri, client_id; codes are single-use and last 60 seconds. grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code takes device_code, client_id and answers authorization_pending, slow_down, expired_token, or access_denied until approved. The access_token is a normal pst_ API token.

post.description: Up to 100 API requests in order as the caller. Body {requests:[{method,path,body,idempotency_key}],stop_on_error}. Returns {results:[{status,body}],failed}. Scopes apply per item, X-Dry-Run applies to every item, items are not atomic, and stop_on_error ends results at the first failure. Idempotency-Key goes on each item, not the batch.

get.description: Validate a loopback request for the dashboard /authorize page without deciding it. Query client_id, redirect_uri, code_challenge, code_challenge_method, state, scope (response_type is accepted and ignored). Requires the approve scope. Returns {client_id, scopes, redirect_uri} as the server normalized them; a scope other than read or write is 400 invalid_scope.

post.description: Loopback consent, called by the dashboard /authorize page that pursuit auth login opens. Requires a signed-in human session with the approve scope (not the PURSUIT_TRUST_PROXY_AUTH owner), Content-Type application/json, and Sec-Fetch-Site same-origin or an Origin matching the host. Writes an oauth.approve or oauth.deny audit entry. Body {client_id, redirect_uri, code_challenge, code_challenge_method:S256, state, scope, approve}. redirect_uri must be http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback or http://[::1]:<port>/callback. Returns {redirect_to}: the callback with code and state, or error=access_denied when approve is false.

get.description: Look up a pending device login by user_code (query) so the dashboard can show the requested scopes. Requires the approve scope. Returns {user_code, client_id, scopes, status, created_at, expires_at, requested_from} (requested_from is the IP that started the login).

post.description: Approve or deny a device login from the dashboard /device page. Body {user_code, approve}. Requires a signed-in human session with the approve scope (not the PURSUIT_TRUST_PROXY_AUTH owner), Content-Type application/json, and Sec-Fetch-Site same-origin or an Origin matching the host; the code alone approves nothing. Writes an oauth.approve or oauth.deny audit entry. Returns {status: approved|denied}.
